name: Kalleigh Sharp
title: Founder & CEO
title_note: Founder & CEO per Kalleigh's 2026 curriculum cover and Vagisha's draft (naeinc.ca page 2834, 22 Oct 2026). Emails to students still sign 'Program Director'.
intro: Kalleigh is the Founder and CEO of the National Association of Estheticians Inc. An entrepreneur, educator and advocate for accessible career education, she writes NAE's curriculum and teaches hair courses at our Richmond Hill beauty school.

sections.heading: About Kalleigh
sections.source: Pink News spotlight 'The Road to Becoming a Beautician' and the Company History post, both on naeinc.ca; degree wording corrected to 'Bachelor of Arts' per Kalleigh's resume ('Tab 1 resume.docx'), sent from NAE's email to Vagisha and Julia, 28 Oct 2026
body: Kalleigh graduated from the University of Guelph with a Bachelor of Arts in 2014. Like a lot of graduates, she left with student debt and spent years working several jobs at once to pay it down.

In 2018 she trained in hair extensions, lash extensions and microblading at Pro Beauty Academy, and started building a client list of her own. With no car, she travelled to clients by transit until her bookings filled up and her debt was paid off.

sections.heading: Her journey
sections.source: Company History post on naeinc.ca (June 2019 meeting); Pink News spotlight
body: In June 2019, Kalleigh sat down with a fellow esthetician and salon owner to talk about a problem they both kept running into. Good beauty training in the region was either in Toronto or expensive, and too often it came with thin course content and little support once the class was over.
They partnered to build NAE around the opposite idea: practical courses taught by people who do the work, at a price a student can manage without taking on debt.

sections.heading: Her mission
sections.source: Pink News spotlight: 'I want to help other women get full time jobs without having to take on the debt.'
body: Kalleigh knows what it costs to start over with a loan hanging over you. Her aim is for every NAE student to learn a skill they can build on, without the debt she had to work her way out of.

sections.heading: Her vision
sections.source: Vagisha's draft 'Meet Our Founder', naeinc.ca page 2834 (draft, 22 Oct 2026)
body: Kalleigh built NAE to make professional beauty education more affordable, flexible and accessible: online theory students can work through at home, paired with hands-on, instructor-led workshops at three beauty schools.
Her goal is training that helps people gain practical skills, start their own business and build greater financial independence.

sections.source: 'Student Success Stories for DD.docx', sent from NAE's email 28 Oct 2026. Reworded only to remove a 'leading beautician' superlative.
body: Nicole Viccica took the Microdermabrasion course in fall 2021 and went on to build Skin by Nicole Grace, a natural facial spa at the Rose Manor Bed and Breakfast in Welland. She sees six to eight clients a week alongside her full-time day job, and sells skincare products from her studio.

Katrina Guiducci took the Eyebrow Lamination, Lift and Tint, Microblading, Lash Lift and Tint, and Nail Technician courses in 2024, straight out of high school and without the student debt of a college program. She went from student to intern to NAE's front desk, while running her own home salon, Rose Beauty Studio.

Jane Refeza completed the Nail Technician course in summer 2023 and Lash Extensions in winter 2024. A mom in St. Catharines, she opened Nail Adix in her basement, now sees about 12 clients a week, and has since moved into a custom salon on her home's main floor, setting her own hours around her family.
